rows.grounds: first member of compound with siddhiḥ, indicating totality
complete attainment or success; head of compound sarva-siddhiḥ
first member of compound with pucche, denoting pervasion or entry
terminal part or end; locative in compound viṣṭi-pucche
qualifies viṣṭi-pucche, indicating a firm or settled state

items.question: What condition allows complete accomplishment to result in lasting stability?
premises: Complete accomplishment is associated with the tail of entry.
The tail of entry can be in a stable state.
Stability arises when that state is stable.
items.inference: Therefore, when the tail of entry is stable, complete accomplishment yields stability.
uncertainties: The precise technical sense of viṣṭi-pucche in this context is unclear.
items.plain_english: All accomplishment is in the tail of entry; but when that tail is stable, stability arises.
